rows.name: level_timer_digits
rows.notes: The TIME countdown, three BCD bytes, most-significant first: 0x07F8 = hundreds, 0x07F9 = tens, 0x07FA = ones. In World 1-1 the paused HUD read TIME 310 and RAM read [3,1,0]. Found with no reference by differential search while Mario stood still: snapshot t0, 150 idle frames, snapshot t1, diff 'decreased' left 21 survivors including 0x07F9 (8->7) and 0x07FA (4->3); a second 150-frame round with from=dt1 narrowed to 6 including 0x07F9. Proof by write: wrote 0x07F8-0x07FA = [5,0,0] (500), the game's own tick decremented it once, and the screenshot HUD showed TIME 499 (naturally it was at 099). The timer only redraws its digits on a tick, so the write must be followed by one tick.

rows.name: score_digits
rows.notes: The displayed MARIO score, six BCD bytes most-significant first: 0x07DD = millions, 0x07DE = hundred-thousands, 0x07DF = ten-thousands, 0x07E0 = thousands, 0x07E1 = hundreds, 0x07E2 = tens. The ones digit is a fixed '0' tile, so the HUD shows seven digits. Found with no reference by differential search: collecting a ? block coin adds exactly 200, and a diff 'increased' (c0->c1, 264 survivors) filtered 'equals 2' left 15 addresses including 0x07E1 (old 0 new 2); the repeat coin on the restarted level (1 coin -> 2, score 200->400) filtered 'equals 4' left 3 including 0x07E1 (old 2 new 4). Proof by write: wrote 0x07DD-0x07E2 = [1,2,3,4,5,6], then collected a coin; the HUD redrew to 1234760 - the written digits 1,2,3,4,6 appear and only the hundreds digit moved 5->7 for the coin's +200, read back as [1,2,3,4,7,6]. The HUD redraws the score only when it changes, so a write needs a score-changing event (a coin) to appear.

rows.name: coin_count_display
rows.notes: The two-digit coin counter shown after the coin icon ('x'), two BCD bytes: 0x07ED = tens, 0x07EE = ones. Found with no reference by differential search: a ? block coin increments only the ones digit, so a diff 'increased' (c0->c1, 264 survivors) filtered 'equals 1' left 32 including 0x07EE (old 0 new 1); the repeat coin (1 -> 2, 'x01' -> 'x02') filtered 'equals 2' left 17 including 0x07EE (old 1 new 2). Proof by write: wrote 0x07ED/0x07EE = [5,5] (would display x55), then collected one coin; the HUD redrew to x56 - the tens 5 is exactly what was written and the ones ticked 5->6, and RAM read back [5,6]. The display only redraws on a change, so the coin had to be collected after the write. Companion binary counter (not displayed) at 0x075E.

rows.name: coin_count_binary
rows.notes: Binary coin counter (0-99; at 100 it resets to 0 and grants a 1-UP) kept alongside the displayed BCD digits at 0x07ED/0x07EE. Found with no reference by the same differential search: after one ? block coin, 'equals 1' over the increased set left it (old 0 new 1); after a second coin, 'equals 2' left it again (old 1 new 2), so it tracks coins one-for-one. Confirmed by write: set 0x075E = 7, collected one coin, read back 8. It is not shown on the HUD; use 0x07ED/0x07EE to change what the player sees.

rows.name: HUD counter extents proven by one-byte-past probes
rows.notes: Extent probes for the three World 1-1 HUD counters (differential search, no reference). Score: wrote 0x07DC..0x07E4 = [9,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8] then collected a ? block coin. RAM read back [0,1,2,3,4,7,6,7,8] and the nametable score row showed tiles [1,2,3,4,7,6,0] - my 0x07DD..0x07E2 digits 1,2,3,4,6 displayed (5 -> 7 for the coin's +200) but 0x07E3 = 7 did NOT appear; the 7th displayed digit stayed the fixed '0' tile. So the stored score is exactly 0x07DD..0x07E2 (six BCD bytes, millions..tens) and the HUD draws a fixed 0 ones digit after it. Coin: wrote 0x07EC..0x07EF = [9,5,5,8] then collected a coin; RAM [9,5,6,8] and the HUD showed x56 - 0x07EC=9 and 0x07EF=8 were not displayed, so the coin display is exactly 0x07ED (tens) / 0x07EE (ones). Timer: wrote 0x07F8..0x07FA = [5,0,0] and the HUD followed to 499, the three visible TIME digits.
